quirks.summary: The request body's root element is LifecycleConfiguration while the model names the payload shape BucketLifecycleConfiguration; a decoder keyed on the shape name would refuse every document a real client sends.

evidence.summary: The documented request syntax opens with a LifecycleConfiguration root element even though the payload member's shape is named BucketLifecycleConfiguration.

quirks.summary: The write demands an integrity claim on the body, so a request with neither Content-MD5 nor an x-amz-checksum header is refused with 400 before the document is parsed.

evidence.summary: The request documents Content-MD5 as required for this operation, which the model spells as a request checksum requirement.

quirks.summary: Unknown elements inside the request document are skipped rather than refused, because a stored configuration parsed more strictly on the next release silently turns lifecycle rules off and the first symptom is objects that stop expiring.

evidence.summary: AWS ignores unknown elements in request XML, and upstream had to relax its decoder to match after strict parsing broke real clients.
The upstream fix that makes unknown request elements a skip rather than an error, which is the behaviour this decoder generates by construction.

quirks.summary: A Filter carries at most one direct child; several conditions must nest inside one And element, and an And with fewer than two conditions is refused as MalformedXML.

evidence.summary: The filter's members are documented as mutually exclusive alternatives, with the And member as the one spelling for combining more than one condition.
The lifecycle rules guide requires multiple filter conditions to be wrapped in a single And element.

quirks.summary: A rule may still scope itself with the deprecated rule-level Prefix element instead of a Filter, because configurations stored under the pre-Filter API revision must keep parsing; a rule carrying neither is refused as MalformedXML.

evidence.summary: The rule's Prefix member is documented as deprecated but still accepted, and Filter is documented as required exactly when the rule carries no Prefix.

quirks.summary: A Date value in an Expiration or Transition action must name midnight UTC; any other time of day is refused with 400 InvalidArgument rather than rounded.

evidence.summary: The Date member is documented as ISO 8601 with the time component always midnight UTC.
The transition's Date member carries the same always-midnight-UTC constraint as the expiration's.

quirks.summary: Days, Date and ExpiredObjectDeleteMarker are mutually exclusive within one Expiration action; a document naming two of them is refused as MalformedXML.

evidence.summary: The ExpiredObjectDeleteMarker member is documented as unusable together with Days or Date, which makes the three members alternatives rather than companions.

quirks.summary: A configuration carries at most 1,000 rules; the 1,001st is refused with 400 rather than truncated or stored.

evidence.summary: The lifecycle rules guide caps a configuration at 1,000 rules per bucket.

quirks.summary: A rule id is at most 255 characters and unique across the configuration; a longer or duplicated id is refused with 400 InvalidArgument.

evidence.summary: The ID member is documented as a unique identifier for the rule with a length cap of 255 characters.

quirks.summary: An expiration measured in days must be a positive integer; zero and negative values are refused with 400 InvalidArgument.

evidence.summary: The Days member is documented as a non-zero positive integer.

quirks.summary: A Status outside the documented Enabled/Disabled pair is stored and echoed rather than refused, because a stored configuration must survive reparse by a stricter release; the fail-open cost of refusing is silently disabled lifecycle rules.

evidence.summary: The Status member documents Enabled and Disabled as its value set, and this project's decision to pass rather than refuse out-of-set spellings is recorded here.
Upstream's lifecycle configuration types could not round-trip stored documents, which is the failure mode a strict enum decode reintroduces.
